questions.q: How does the summary suggest finding a fulfilling career?
a: Match your existing skills to the lifestyle you want
Follow whatever passion you felt strongest as a child
Choose the field with the highest entry-level salary
Wait until a dream job appears and then apply
questions.why: Lesson 1 says examining the lifestyle you desire and your skills matters more than passion alone.

questions.q: What did Bill McKibben’s example show about job satisfaction?
a: Impact and a flexible lifestyle can matter more than loving the craft itself
Writing talent is innate and cannot be developed through practice
Journalism is only fulfilling for people who enjoy research
A prestigious newspaper job is the surest route to happiness
questions.why: Lesson 1 says McKibben valued his positive influence and flexible hours, and built his writing skill over years.

a: Wanting to prove you are capable, which leads to stagnation
Seeking constant improvement by studying better people
Comparing your progress only with your past self
Avoiding feedback so your confidence stays intact
questions.why: Lesson 2 says a be-good attitude focuses on proving capability and leaves little room to grow.

a: Measuring yourself against your past self and seeking improvement
Comparing your results with the people around you
Sticking to tasks you already perform well
Avoiding difficult work that could expose mistakes
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the get-better attitude focuses on daily improvement rather than comparison with others.

questions.q: What did Coca-Cola’s expansion into East Germany illustrate?
a: Opportunity often requires accepting risk despite possible pitfalls
Large companies should avoid unfamiliar markets entirely
Every risky expansion eventually produces a loss
Only unanimous leadership teams make good decisions
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the team overcame fear, took the risk and built a profitable market despite difficulties.
